To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we generated a stable, long-term, and functional human T-cell response in a mouse model by introducing human hematopoietict stem cells (hSCs) expressing an HLA-restricted T-cell receptor (TCR) into a humanized mouse model.
we generated functional tumor-specific human CD8+ T-cells in vivo from genetically manipulated human hematopoietetic stem cells.

the use of genetically engineered human hematopietic stem cells expressing a high affinity melanoma-specific T cell receptor resulted in the generation of functional melanoma specific CD8+ T-cells that were able to limit and clear human melanoma tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic approach to treat cancer.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for cancer immunotherapy based on gene transfer into human stem cells.
the generation and use of antigen-specific T cells for cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that it is possible to generate an antitumor T cell in vivo from genetically enhanced HSC.
we have shown that genetically engineered human hematopietic stem cells can be used to generate functional tumor-specific T cells in vivo that are capable of controlling and eradicating tumors.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using genetically modified hHSC to generate tumor-reactive human CD8+ T lymphocytes in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of generating functional human T cells from genetically engineered human HSC in vivo.
we have developed a new strategy to generate antitumor CD8 T cells from genetically modified human HSCs in vivo.
we have shown that we could generate an effective, stable and self-renewable population of tumor-specific CD8 T-cells from genetically engineered human HSCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have generated an antitumor T cell from a human hematopoietically stem cell that can be used for adoptive transfer.
it is possible to generate a stable population of melanoma-specific CD8 T-cells in the absence of any ex vivo expansion.
we were able to generate functional tumor-specific human CD8+ T lymphocytes from genetically modified hematopoietic progenitors in a mouse model.
